description: One named agent, in `./.dive/agents/` or `~/.config/dive/agents/`. A file with a built-in agent's name replaces that agent everywhere it runs.

examples.description: Answers questions about what shipped, from the repo's commit history.
examples.name: release_notes
examples.system_prompt:
You answer questions about what shipped in this repository.
Today's date: {{session.date}}

attachments.description: No longer used. Dive accepts and ignores it, and `dive config check` notes it. Every agent sees whatever the thread has loaded, and what it can do comes only from its `tools`; a thread loads a network draft or evidence when an agent calls `builtin__create_network`, `builtin__open_network` or `builtin__attach_evidence`, or when you open an edit thread.

description.description: What the agent is for, written for the people and agents choosing it.

handoffs.description: Agents this one can hand the conversation to, called as `transfer_to_<name>`. An agent can't hand off to itself, and an agent handed the conversation gets `transfer_back` without listing it.

input_schema.description: Typed input when the agent runs as a subagent or plan step. An object schema with a `description` on every property. Without it, a call takes `{prompt}`.

max_iterations.description: A cap on model rounds. Omitted means no cap as a subagent; in a conversation, `[settings].max_agent_iterations` applies.

model.description: The model role the agent runs on, standard (`chat`) or custom.

name.description: Starts with a lowercase letter; lowercase letters, digits and `_` only. Other agents and plan steps call it as `agent__<name>`.

output_schema.description: Typed output when the agent runs as a subagent or plan step. An object schema. Without it, a call returns the final reply as `{result}`.

subagents.description: Agents this one can run as a subagent, each in a fresh context, called as `agent__<name>`. Listing the agent's own name lets it run a fresh copy of itself. Nesting is capped at 3.

system_prompt.description: The agent's instructions, rendered with the template language. It can reference `{{session.date}}`, `{{session.user}}` and the `{{rules.*}}` blocks (`control_steps`, `composing`, `templating`, `tool_format`, `agent_format`, `design`), and nothing else. `{{session.date}}` is today's date with no time of day, so the prompt stays the same all day and a resumed thread keeps its prompt cache.

tools.description: Catalog tools the agent may call, as exact names or `*` globs such as `linear__*`. `[]` means none and `["*"]` means the whole catalog. Control step names and generated `agent__` and `transfer_to_` names aren't allowed. A name that matches no tool, such as a tool from a pack that isn't installed, is skipped, so the agent still loads and runs without it. The tools aren't loaded up front. The agent gets `plan__search_tools`, which searches only this list, and each tool a search returns stays loaded for the rest of the thread. Handoffs, subagents, the workbench tools the list names in full, and the `[tools].always_loaded` tools the list matches are loaded from the start; a workbench tool matched only by a glob such as `*` is found by search like any other. Naming `plan__search_tools` here makes its search cover the whole catalog as well as this list, for agents that find tools for others.

version.description: The file version the document is written in. Omitted means 1; files Dive writes always carry it.
